title: The Power of Opportunity and Support

content.text: National Inclusion Week returns from 14th to 20th September 2026 and it’s a valuable opportunity for us to recognise the difference that access to the right opportunity and the right support can make to the start of someone’s career.

For many people, the route into employment is not straightforward. Going Forward into Employment (GFiE) is about helping to open those doors, creating opportunities for people who may face barriers to employment and providing routes into meaningful work that can build confidence, skills and experience.

GFiE shows what can happen when recruitment is approached differently. Across its pathways, people from a wide range of backgrounds bring their skills, experiences and potential into the Civil Service. The focus is not simply on getting someone into a role, but on giving them the support they need to make a positive start and develop in employment.

That support can make a real difference. GFiE provides opportunities to learn and grow for candidates, managers and buddies, with mentoring and practical support helping people navigate their early experiences in the workplace.
Don't just take our word for it
We recently caught up with a Civil Service colleague who volunteers as a GFiE Buddy to hear first hand about the impact this can have for both candidates and volunteers.

Buddies are an incredibly important part of our work and if you are a Civil Service colleague who would like to become a buddy please do email us at gfie@cabinetoffice.gov.uk. We can tell you more about the role and the training we provide

GFiE’s impact is about more than filling vacancies. It is about recognising potential, creating opportunities that might otherwise be missed, and helping people take their next step with the confidence and support to succeed.
